references.text: Sarai gives her servant Hagar to Abram to have children through her, a parallel action to Rachel's decision to give her servant to Jacob.
Leah gives her servant Zilpah to Jacob as a wife to have children through her, mirroring Rachel's action.
Lists the twelve sons of Jacob, including those born to the servants, emphasizing the significance of Rachel's and Leah's actions in building the twelve tribes of Israel.
Joseph sees Ephraim's children in the third generation, and Makir's sons were born "on Joseph's knees" – the same expression Rachel uses regarding giving birth "on my knees".
Sarai gives Hagar to Abram as a wife, a direct parallel to Rachel's action in the next verse (Gen 30:4) where she gives Bilhah to Jacob.
Genesis 29:29 establishes the historical and personal context that makes Rachel's request in 30:3 possible.
